title: Simplified behavioural tests for transient social memory in male mice and dams
protocol: Transfer mice from group housing to individual housing at age 40-50 days for 5 days.
Introduce a stimulus female into the home cage of a male mouse for a 1-minute interaction.
Remove the stimulus animal after the 1-minute trial and return the male to an individual holding cage.
Score behavior during the experiment and record on videotape.
Wait 10 minutes before introducing the same stimulus female again for another 1-minute interaction with the male.
Remove the stimulus animal after the second 1-minute trial and return the male to the individual holding cage.
Wait 10 minutes and introduce the same stimulus female for a third 1-minute interaction with the male.
Remove the stimulus animal after the third 1-minute trial and return the male to the individual holding cage.
Wait 10 minutes and introduce the same stimulus female for a fourth 1-minute interaction with the male.
Introduce a new stimulus female for another 1-minute interaction with the male.
Introduce a different stimulus female to the same male mouse for 1 min.
Wait for a 10-min inter-exposure interval before introducing the stimulus female.
Record the investigation time of the female by the male during each trial.
Remove the stimulus animal and place it in an individual holding cage after the interaction.
Observe each new dam for 5 min to confirm births on Day 1.
Confirm that the dam is capable of building a typical nest with pups present on Day 1.
Remove all of the pups from the nest and keep them temporarily in a holding cage on Day 2.
Return five of the dam's own pups to the dam's cage, placing them at the opposite side from the nest on Day 2.
Observe the dam continually for up to 3 min to record latency to retrieve each pup to the nest on Day 2.
Repeat step 4 three times to ensure accurate recording of retrieval behavior on Day 2.
